Generally, if something already has a spot in the Action Order, something new adding to it will let them act. If something adds a new group, it can't act until the next round in the Action Order. (Though the GM can still introduce surprises on the heroes by not showing all the minion groups until applicable during the first round in the Action Order.)

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
You have the Attack action right, but not Defend. Defend is a proactive normal action that reduces the amount of damage taken before your next action. You can choose yourself or someone else to Defend (at the time you take the action).

You can also “hit the deck” as a Reaction to Defend yourself only, but doing so inflicts a Minor Twist–it’s effectively already a Risky Action. I’d personally rule that extending that to use “hit the deck” on an ally should be used sparingly, if at all, would require a vivid description, and would incur a Major Twist instead of a minor one, but that’s just me.

posts.name: NestorDRod
posts.cooked:
But that's what I mean, Defend is a proactive action, i.e. you choose it before an attack takes place. The concept I'm thinking of is the classic scene in movies and books where the hero leaps in to intercept the attack at the last minute as he becomes aware of it. The Defend action implies the character is standing ready, waiting for an attack to come in, like a goalie guarding the net.

A risky action is still a basic action, i.e. it takes place on your turn, so that approach doesn't fit the concept either.

I suppose extending Hit the Deck to apply to an ally by requiring a Major Twist could be a feasible solution; I could see having the intercepting hero taking their Max die in damage for their heroism.

I don't know, the whole thing comes across as more of a gamist approach to the genre, as opposed to simulationist.

As a GM you should use whichever die or amount of damage you think is appropriate to the scene and the situation. Risky Actions can be thought of like other games do Stunts or other on-the-fly moves, just instead of there being a penalty to your die roll or whatever you take a Minor Twist because it's not something you're doing regularly (which is what an Ability is.)
